entries.speaker: george-clanton
entries.heard: I'm going to start from the top. My true north, The Velvet Underground, of course. I picked this one in particular. This is Loaded.
entries.quote: I'm going to start from the top. My true north, The Velvet Underground, of course. I picked this one in particular. This is Loaded.
entries.note: Speaker is Brad of TV Girl (he says he pitched the project to George); not George Clanton. Praise only, no tie to his own music.

entries.speaker: george-clanton
entries.heard: George is going to hate this one, so I
entries.quote: George is going to hate this one, so I had to get the Malcolm McLaren Sex Pistols poster cuz
entries.note: Speaker is Brad of TV Girl, buying a poster; no influence claim.

entries.speaker: the-last-dinner-party
entries.speakerName: A member of The Last Dinner Party
entries.heard: kind of everything I have a guitar I play her guitar my dad introduced her to me probably when I was about like 14
entries.quote: I have a guitar, I play her guitar. My dad introduced her to me, probably when I was about, like, 14.
entries.citation: A member of The Last Dinner Party says on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag? of St. Vincent: "I have a guitar, I play her guitar. My dad introduced her to me, probably when I was about, like, 14."
entries.note: Which member speaks is unclear. Preceded by 'we are very big St. Vincent fans in this band'. Second album = Actor. Moderate: fandom tied to formative years and playing her guitar.

entries.speaker: the-last-dinner-party
entries.speakerName: A member of The Last Dinner Party
entries.record: Nick Drake tribute compilation (they cover 'Cello Song')
entries.heard: Drake covers record um cuz I love fontaine's DC and I saw that they covered Cello Song
entries.quote: I love Fontaines D.C., and I saw that they covered 'Cello Song'.
entries.note: Picked for Fontaines' cover on a Nick Drake tribute; nick-drake not judged (cover record).

entries.speaker: black-country-new-road
entries.speakerName: A member of Black Country, New Road
entries.heard: I really like the production on the album I think it's so good I think just like the way the band play and the way
entries.quote: I really like the production on the album. I think it's so good.
entries.note: Album title mis-captioned; 'a long drive for someone with nothing to think about' is from Modest Mouse's 'Trailer Trash'... likely The Lonesome Crowded West (record not certain). Praise only.

entries.speaker: black-country-new-road
entries.speakerName: A member of Black Country, New Road
entries.heard: maybe the kind of bread and butter of my existence existence I maybe listen to this sometimes both in a day every day every
entries.quote: Maybe the kind of bread and butter of my existence. I maybe listen to this sometimes both in a day, every day.
entries.note: Artist not named in the captions; inferred from 'Time, as a Symptom' and 'Have One on Me' (Joanna Newsom). Praise/listening habit, no tie to the band's own music.

entries.speaker: husker-du
entries.record: Another Music in a Different Kitchen
entries.heard: the first buzz cox album another music in a different kitchen peach shelley is like one of the main influences on my work buzzcocks i'm sure
entries.quote: The first Buzzcocks album, Another Music in a Different Kitchen. Pete Shelley is like one of the main influences on my work.
entries.citation: Bob Mould of Hüsker Dü says on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag? of Buzzcocks' first album: "Pete Shelley is like one of the main influences on my work."
entries.note: Buzzcocks' Another Music in a Different Kitchen is 1978, Mould heard them live in Minnesota autumn 1978 (before Hüsker Dü).

entries.speaker: husker-du
entries.heard: i mean this is a this one changed everything for me i think it changed everything for anybody who heard it
entries.quote: I mean, this one changed everything for me. I think it changed everything for anybody who heard it.
entries.citation: Bob Mould of Hüsker Dü says on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag? of My Bloody Valentine's Loveless: "this one changed everything for me. I think it changed everything for anybody who heard it."
entries.note: Heard Dec 1991, after Hüsker Dü split (1988): it shaped his later work, not the band's. Also says 'for me it's like Loveless and then this' at 8:32.

entries.speaker: the-postal-service
entries.heard: videos of the process and every time i watched one of the videos it would make me want to go work on my own stuff and besides that
entries.quote: ...videos of the process, and every time I watched one of the videos it would make me want to go work on my own stuff.
entries.citation: Jimmy Tamborello (Dntel, The Postal Service) says on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag? that Charli XCX's lockdown videos for how i'm feeling now "would make me want to go work on my own stuff."
entries.note: Introduced as 'speaking of inspiration'. Inspires his current work (2020); Postal Service far earlier. Quote is trimmed from the sentence's start.

entries.speaker: sonic-youth
entries.heard: like sort of noise slide guitar and it was it was just absolutely amazing. It really reduced rock back to its essentials in like the most fantastic
entries.quote: Lydia was just playing like sort of noise slide guitar and it was just absolutely amazing. It really reduced rock back to its essentials in the most fantastic way.
entries.note: Speaks of the No New York bands collectively (Teenage Jesus, Contortions, Mars, DNA, all already linked); worn-out copies, but no stated tie to his own music.

entries.speaker: sonic-youth
entries.heard: I saw Talking Heads in their their very earliest days when they were touring in a station wagon, touring little towns in New York and
entries.quote: I saw Talking Heads in their very earliest days when they were touring in a station wagon, touring little towns in New York and was completely hooked.
entries.note: Fan from their earliest days, but no claim about his own music or Sonic Youth.

entries.speaker: alvvays
entries.heard: I'm a big fan of of the fall and uh this is probably my favorite record from them
entries.quote: I'm a big fan of the Fall, and this is probably my favorite record from them.
entries.note: Big fan, no tie to her own music.

entries.speaker: waxahatchee
entries.heard: I mean, Lucinda Williams is a whole thing for Allison and I. She's probably my favorite songwriter of all time and
entries.quote: I mean, Lucinda Williams is a whole thing for Allison and I. She's probably my favorite songwriter of all time...
entries.note: Speaker is Katie ('Allison and I'). Says she discovered Lucinda later in life and 'hadn't spent a lot of time with this record'; no tie to her music.

entries.speaker: waxahatchee
entries.heard: I got Songs: Ohia, one of my favorite albums as of recently. People have sort of talked to me about Jason Molina's music for as long as I can remember but I sort of slept on his music for a long time and recently I've just had such a moment with this record.
entries.quote: I got Songs: Ohia, one of my favorite albums as of recently. People have sort of talked to me about Jason Molina's music for as long as I can remember, but I sort of slept on his music for a long time...
entries.note: Speaker not clear; either way a recent discovery (favourite at most).

entries.speaker: waxahatchee
entries.heard: I picked 'Heaven or Las Vegas' by the Cocteau Twins. Predictably you picked... Predictably, yeah. I listened to it constantly when I was making my record 'Tourist in This Town'
entries.quote: I picked 'Heaven or Las Vegas' by the Cocteau Twins. Predictably you picked... Predictably, yeah. I listened to it constantly when I was making my record 'Tourist in This Town'
entries.note: 'Tourist in This Town' is Allison Crutchfield's solo album, not Waxahatchee: speaker is Allison (not on the map). Would be influence if it were Katie.

entries.speaker: waxahatchee
entries.heard: This is Tobin Sprout from Guided By Voices' solo album 'Moonflower Plastic.' It's a really, really great record, cover to cover.
entries.quote: This is Tobin Sprout from Guided By Voices' solo album 'Moonflower Plastic.' It's a really, really great record, cover to cover.
entries.note: Speaker not clear; Sprout solo record, praise only.

entries.speaker: nirvana
entries.heard: You've got No Means No, one of my favorite bands, from Victoria, Canada They were....besides the Bad Brains No Means No were the best hard hardcore band ever. I think. Live. They were amazing.
entries.quote: You've got NoMeansNo, one of my favorite bands, from Victoria, Canada. Besides the Bad Brains, NoMeansNo were the best hardcore band ever, I think. Live, they were amazing.
entries.note: Praise for the band live, spoken while looking at a comp; no tie to Nirvana's music.

entries.speaker: kurt-vile
entries.heard: This is a another must. This guy's my hero. I think he's the greatest living American songwriter. John Prine and this is his first album. Do you have it? Maybe Jen has it but now you have your own copy.
entries.quote: This is another must. This guy's my hero. I think he's the greatest living American songwriter. John Prine and this is his first album.
entries.note: Speaker probably Kurt (picking for Courtney; 'Jen' is Courtney's partner); 'my hero' with no tie to his own music.

entries.speaker: kurt-vile
entries.heard: Alright, this is my favorite record by this iconic sad artist. Country/folk artist Townes Van Zandt. Do you have any of his records?
entries.quote: Alright, this is my favorite record by this iconic sad artist. Country/folk artist Townes Van Zandt.
entries.note: Probably Kurt picking for Courtney; praise only.

entries.speaker: kurt-vile
entries.record: Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill
entries.heard: Ok, this... I was actually looking for her latest album but it's out of stock. But this is the first one I heard. This is Grouper. This very cool, kind of shy experimental girl.
entries.quote: Okay, this... I was actually looking for her latest album but it's out of stock. But this is the first one I heard. This is Grouper.
entries.note: Who is picking is unclear; praise only.

entries.speaker: kurt-vile
entries.heard: You've probably got this, right? Do you have this? 'The Woods?' Sleater-Kinney? I figured because we're touring with Janet. But I love it, and my favorite song 'A Modern Girl' is on it.
entries.quote: You've probably got this, right? Do you have this? 'The Woods'? Sleater-Kinney? I figured because we're touring with Janet. But I love it, and my favorite song 'A Modern Girl' is on it.
entries.note: Speaker unclear (likely Courtney); praise only.

entries.speaker: ariel-pink
entries.heard: bucks yeah these guys what can you say about them that hasn't already been said nakam Mooney was my first show in La think I was underage but I managed to
entries.quote: Yeah, these guys, what can you say about them that hasn't already been said? Malcolm Mooney was my first show in LA, I think I was underage, but I managed to...
entries.note: Captions garbled ('nakam Mooney'); first LA show with Malcolm Mooney; 'if my mom hadn't given birth to me I wouldn't have ever heard Can'. No stated tie to his music.

entries.speaker: mac-demarco
entries.heard: I love Jonathon. Huge inspiration for me. Really cool.
entries.quote: I love Jonathan. Huge inspiration for me. Really cool.
entries.citation: Mac DeMarco says on Amoeba Music's What's In My Bag?, of Jonathan Richman and The Modern Lovers: "I love Jonathan. Huge inspiration for me."
entries.note: The inspiration line follows a story about watching Jonathan Richman at FYF; also 'classic for me, love it' on the album at 1:49. Refers to Jonathan Richman himself, the Modern Lovers' leader.

entries.speaker: car-seat-headrest
entries.heard: New Kurt Cobain collection also supposed to be really bad but, again, 12 year old me would've eaten it up
entries.quote: New Kurt Cobain collection, also supposed to be really bad, but again 12-year-old me would've eaten it up.
entries.note: Solo Cobain collection, not the band. 'Would've eaten it up' implies childhood fandom but is not an influence claim.

entries.speaker: big-star
entries.heard: Ah let's see, Elliot Smith. I came to Amoeba here a few years ago and I had to buy a Big Star CD for someone
entries.quote: Ah, let's see, Elliott Smith. I came to Amoeba here a few years ago and I had to buy a Big Star CD for someone
entries.note: No praise: anecdote about Elliott Smith's sister and a recording session together (collaboration). The influence ran Big Star to Elliott, not the reverse.

entries.speaker: black-flag
entries.heard: Tick Demon's claws chick chick chick miscellaneous
entries.quote: Tick, Demon's Claws, Chk Chk Chk, miscellaneous...
entries.note: Caption 'chick chick chick' probably !!!; a bare purchase list, no comment.

offMap.speaker: the-last-dinner-party
offMap.quote: That kind of got me into this, and yeah, I just went through a massive phase of trying to learn the songs.

offMap.speaker: black-country-new-road

offMap.speaker: black-country-new-road
offMap.quote: Probably quite inspiring to me when I was like learning to play the saxophone. I want to sound like him as much as possible.

offMap.speaker: explosions-in-the-sky

offMap.speaker: the-postal-service
offMap.quote: I've gotten a lot of inspiration from this photo in the album of his little studio setup.

offMap.speaker: alvvays

offMap.speaker: waxahatchee

offMap.speaker: nirvana
